sanjay_procure: Vendor update — H100 shipment ETA pushed to 2025-05-16 due to linehaul congestion. They want to hold 20% of the batch in escrow until RMA resolution window closes. Do we accept or push for alternate forwarder? :thinking:

maria_ops: Ouch. That pushes our available capacity for the east cluster below the SLA for the week. Can we route some jobs to the dedicated pool in IAD as a stopgap?

linda_logistics: @maria_ops we can route ~48 GPUs from the reserve pool but that'll eat the buffer for May. Escrow note: vendor requires escrow payment wired to their forwarder account, plus AWB holds until customs clears.

alex_research: If we lose those GPUs for two weeks we're running 15% higher tail latency on long seqs. We should avoid if possible. Any cheaper expedite option from the vendor?

sanjay_procure: Vendor offered a conditional leaseback on 10 units (loaner) if DOA rate > 3% on arrival — expires at ETD. Expedited air costs +$220k for the batch. Alternate forwarder quote is +$70k but 3 days faster.

rma-bot: Note — previous batch 1736012345 had DOA rate 1.1%, average RMA turnaround 7 business days (depot EU). Escrow clause applied once in 2024-09.

maria_ops: Two tradeoffs: pay expedite (+$220k) to avoid cluster falloff, or switch forwarder (+$70k) and accept 3 day lead improvement but risk customs holdup. Which has faster certainty?

linda_logistics: Switching forwarder reduces transit days but vendor warns that new paperwork flow may trigger duplicate customs checks because shipment re-declared — extra hold risk. Escrow only kicks in when vendor sees missing manifest items.

tyler_finance: From budget POV, the extra $70k is preferable. Can you get a written SLA from the alternate forwarder on transit time and customs handling? If not, finance prefers expedite to guarantee availability.

alex_research: Also note network constraint: the east cluster currently has a partial fiber degradation on the DC crosslink (10G bonding flaps), we will lose some aggregate throughput if we re-route to IAD. Ops has a mitigation but it needs 4 hours of maintenance.

maria_ops: We prefer not to do maintenance during the ML training blackout window. If we accept alternate forwarder we need a 24h contingency to flip routing and keep latency SLOs.

sanjay_procure: Proposed plan: 1) Ask alternate forwarder for SLA + written customs handling guarantee (48h max hold). 2) If they agree, pay forwarder (+$70k). 3) If they decline, approve vendor expedite (+$220k) and accept 20% escrow with conditions: escrow released after 14 days post-delivery with clear serial reconciliation. Thoughts?

tyler_finance: OK to pre-approve up to $120k from contingency fund for this month. Anything above needs exec signoff. So we can greenlight the +$70k option if SLA arrives in writing.

linda_logistics: I'll ping forwarder and request the written SLA and customs handling workflow. ETA for response 4 hours.

alex_research: If forwarder SLA looks weak then we should also schedule the 4h maintenance window for the crosslink as contingency (after-hours). Ops to provide exact window.

maria_ops: Agreed. @linda_logistics please include the escrow release language & serial reconciliation steps in the response so procurement can evaluate legal risk.

sanjay_procure: Will loop in legal if escrow wording looks bad. Also requesting vendor to confirm depot RMA contact and expedited replacement S/N list in advance (we want pre-built return labels).

linda_logistics: Got it — pinging now.

rma-bot: FYI — best practice from prior incidents: include `AWB`, `serial manifest`, and `depot contact` in first-day packet. That reduces RMA triage by ~2 days.

maria_ops: Thanks. Keep updates here. If forwarder SLA arrives and is solid, mark approved and finance will auto-release. If not, we escalate to execs for expedite approval. :thumbsup:
